FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 6 April 1989, after the draft finalized by the Jute and Jute Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. Various types of flexible bags, such as, multiwall paper bags, double laminated jute and HDPE woven fabric bags, etc, are being used for packing milk powder in the country. These bags are required not only to protect the milk powder from contamination and moisture but also to withstand the hazards of handling and transportation. The laminated jute bags covered in this standard are used for packing milk powder which is meant for direct consumption in bulk. Milk powder packed in such bags is used only for conversion into other products in dairies or food industries. The quantity generally packed is 25 kg. However, such packages are required to be stored at temperature below 20' C. These bags are also used for bulk packing of small polyethylene bags containing one or 2 kg milk powder for transportation purposes. The dimensions of the bags specified in this standard are optimum for holding 25 kg of milk powder. The dimensions are corrected for optimum free space of about 25 cm when measured along the surface of the fabric from the mouth stitch line of the bag up to the surface level of the contents. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

The bonding material shall be smoothly and uniformly spread throughout and shall not crack on folding the bags. The adhesion between the plies shall be such that there is no delamination. 4.1.1 Bitumen used for bonding shall be 100 f 30 g/m ' (both sides ) or 50 f 15 g/m" ( one side j as the case may be. Bitumen content shall be determined by the method specified in IS 8477 : 1985. 4.2 Bag The bags shall be of the folIowing types: a) Type I The bags made out of hessian fabric laminated with kraft paper on outer side and plastic fiIm/kraft paper inside using bitumen as the bonding agent and having one liner of kraft paper ( see 3.2 ) or plastic film ( see 3.3 ) stitched along with the bag at the side and the bottom ( See Note ).

4.4.1 The stitching at the side and the bottom of the bags shall be done by two rows of chain or lock stitches using plied yarn of rayon or any other man-made fibre as agreed to between the buyer and the seller and the number of stitches shall be between ~9to 12/dm. The outer stitch shall be approximate!y 10 mm away from the edge of the bag and the two rows of stitches shall be about 5 mm apart. The stitching shall be uniform and without any loose threads or knots. 4.5 Liner The loose liner ( see 3.4 ) shall be used inside the laminated bag. The width of the liner shall be at least 5 cm more than the width of the bag and length shall be at least 20 cm more than the length of the bag. 4.6 The bags shall conform to the requirements as given in Table 1. 5 PACJUNG AND MARKING 5.1 Packing The bags shall be packed in trusses containing SO bags or multiples thereof using hessian fabric for covering and shall be securely stitched. 2

Name of the manufacturer, Description of bags and type, Number of bags per truss, Lot number of the truss, and Any other particulars required by the buyer or by the law or regulation in force.
